label: Women's suffrage introduction year
reliability_criteria: Canonical tier = a curated table of 185 countries, one row each, every row citing the IPU "Women's Suffrage" table entry it was read from. The year is the IPU's date of the right to vote in national elections ON EQUAL TERMS (decision 24, 2026-10-14): when the IPU flags the first grant as restricted and records the restrictions lifted later, the lifted date is kept and the first grant rides the row's definition_note (United Kingdom 1928, Belgium 1948, Portugal 1976, Australia 1962, Canada 1950). Medium, not high: a single compiler for all rows (no per-row cross-check against the statutes), an archive page last updated in 2005, and a convention choice (equal terms, not first grant). Staged grants by population group take the latest stage so that every woman is covered (South Africa 1994, Nigeria 1978); where the IPU lists several dates as stages of one grant (confirmation at independence), the earliest is kept. No witness tier: the Lexical Index of Electoral Democracy (via OWID, "Universal right to vote for women") dates the EFFECTIVE universal right and disagrees with the IPU's legal dates for most countries (2026-10-14 comparison: 68 of 179 matched countries identical, the others mostly one to two years apart, a few by decades - Brazil 1932 against 1985, South Africa 1930 against 1994, Chile 1949 against 1970), a different concept: recorded, not wired.
license: Facts with citation (small extracts, clearly attributed) - see docs/licenses.md and catalog/curated/README.md.
notes: Year women obtained the right to vote in national elections, on equal terms, one row per country (the marker's shape: the point's year = the value). Europe's step, as the table prints it: Finland 1906, Norway 1913, Denmark 1915, Germany 1918, the Netherlands 1919, the United Kingdom 1928, France 1944, Italy 1945, Belgium 1948, Greece 1952, Switzerland 1971, Portugal 1976, Liechtenstein 1984. THE HONEST LIMITS: the equal-terms date is a convention (the first grant is in each row's note); the IPU page is an archive, so recent changes and countries without national elections are absent; Yemen merges two pre-unification dates (Arab Republic 1970, D.P.R. 1967, the later kept); "Yugoslavia" is the historical entity (1946), Serbia and Montenegro have no row.
